result.summary: RECONSTRUCTED HANDOFF -- written 2026-09-03 after the fact; timestamps are reconstructed approximations. Both BLOCKERs independently re-verified against real source and resolved in the design doc, confirmed present on disk at reconstruction time. (1) OQ-3: read Letflow.Webhooks.attempt_loop/7 (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex) directly -- confirmed it freezes subscription.target_url once at the top of the retry loop and never re-renders it on any subsequent attempt, re-validating only. §10 OQ-3 in the design doc now reads 'RESOLVED (was MAJOR/open; resolved during rework per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's BLOCKER finding)', citing this exact precedent. §4.1/§5.2/§5.6 step 2 updated to state explicitly: REQ-215's activation-time caller renders the URL template once, before the first INSERT into service_task_dispatches; this poller re-renders nothing, ever, on any attempt including retries -- it dispatches against the frozen config_snapshot.rendered_url on every attempt, re-validating via UrlValidator.validate/2 fresh each time but never re-rendering. (2) Locking: rewrote §5.4's claim_due_dispatch_ids/2 as a two-step select-then-lock. Step 1 is an unlocked query joining instance_projections for the :active filter and selecting eligible ids -- no lock/1 call anywhere in this query. Step 2 is a second, single-table query on service_task_dispatches only, re-selecting by the Step-1 id list with a bare, unqualified lock("FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED") -- confirmed to mirror Letflow.Scheduler.claim_due_timer_ids/2's own shape exactly (single-table, no join, bare lock). The design doc's own §5.4 states explicitly that a row racing between Step 1 and Step 2 is simply absent from Step 2's SKIP LOCKED result, introducing no new race beyond what the design already accepted, and that a row whose instance is no longer :active is excluded at Step 1 and never reaches Step 2's lock at all -- satisfying the SCH-03-style skip-at-claim-time acceptance criterion. No implementation code was introduced -- both fixes are signatures, a two-step query shown as illustrative Ecto (matching this design doc's own established convention of showing real, verified query shapes without wrapping them in a defp body), and prose. This reconstruction independently re-confirmed, at the time of writing this backfill, that the design doc's current §5.4 and §10 OQ-3 read exactly as described above -- direct textual confirmation, not merely trusting a prior claim.

(2) Claim-query locking specified an invented lock("FOR UPDATE OF d0 SKIP LOCKED") syntax with zero codebase precedent -- every real lock(...) call in this project is a bare, unqualified lock on a single-table (no-join) query.
